Simulate survey data from the model

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_areal.Rd

Draws one realisation of the latent surface on a frame and time frame, then binomial surveys at randomly chosen area-time cells (one survey per cell). The logit prevalence is the fixed effects set by formula (by default an intercept and a linear trend running from -1 at the first time step to 1 at the last) + a Leroux x AR1 field, with a cell-level nugget added at each surveyed cell.

Usage

simulate_areal(
  frame,
  time,
  formula = ~trend(),
  covariates = NULL,
  scale_covariates = TRUE,
  beta = c(-1, 1),
  sigma = 1,
  rho_s = 0.9,
  rho_t = 0.9,
  sigma_n = 0.3,
  n_cells = 100,
  k = 50,
  seed = NULL,
  cells = NULL
)

Arguments

frame

A areal_frame().

time

A time_frame().

formula, covariates, scale_covariates

The fixed effects, as in fit_areal(). Simulating and fitting with the same settings gives effects on the same scale.

beta

Fixed effects on the logit scale: one per design column, in order (intercept, trend if in the formula, then the covariates; see areal_priors()), or named by design column.

sigma

Scale of the field: the standard deviation of the Leroux prior is sigma times a factor set by the graph (\(\tau = 1/\sigma^2\)).

rho_s

Spatial dependence of the Leroux prior, in (0, 1).

rho_t

Lag-one temporal correlation of the AR1, in (0, 1).

sigma_n

Standard deviation of the cell-level nugget (0 for none).

n_cells

Number of distinct area-time cells surveyed, chosen at random.

k

Number tested per survey: one number, or one per cell.

seed

Random seed. If given, the caller's random-number stream is left untouched.

cells

Instead of n_cells random cells: the cells to survey, as a data frame with an area id column, a t (step number) or time (label) column, and optionally k (number tested). The $cells of an areal_data() object qualifies, so a simulation can copy a real survey design: its areas, time steps and sample sizes.

Value

A areal_data() object (stareal_data), ready for fit_areal(), with $truth: theta (natural scale), beta (named by design column), logit and prevalence (areas x time steps matrices of the surface without the nugget; prevalence in percent), x (the logit at each surveyed cell with its nugget, in the order of $cells: what a fit estimates for the observed cells) and design. $surveys has columns id, t, time, date (calendar frames), y, k.

Examples

fr <- areal_lattice(6, 6)
tf <- time_frame(2001, 2020, "year")
sim <- simulate_areal(fr, tf, n_cells = 60, seed = 1)
sim
#> <stareal_data> 60 of 60 surveys used, pooled into 60 cells (simulated)
#>   29 of 36 units and 20 of 20 time steps have data (8.33% of the 720 area-time cells)
#>   tested per cell: median 50, range 50-50; total 3,000 tested, 710 positive
#>   truth: sigma 1, rho_s 0.9, rho_t 0.9, sigma_n 0.3; intercept -1, trend 1
